Finding: Model B appears domain-shifted toward culinary/recipe/restaurant content.

Reasoning:
- In the highest-norm cells (layers ~17–25, especially pos1–pos4), the logit-lens consistently points to cooking terms: “Cook,” “cooking,” “Cooking,” “restaurant/Restaurant,” “baking,” “Chef/chef,” “kitchen/Kitchen,” “microwave,” “oven,” “Cake,” “Baked,” “Baker,” “Professional/professional,” “culinary,” “Mediterranean.”
- This pattern is pervasive across layers and positions where the difference is largest, indicating a semantic, domain-level shift rather than a superficial token effect.
- Earlier mid-layers also show related formal/technical vocabulary (“culinary,” “Restaurant,” “delectable,” “exquisite”) alongside more general formal terms (“dissertation,” “sciences,” “Innovation”), consistent with a professionalized food/recipe style.

Conclusion: Compared to Model A, Model B is biased toward or finetuned on culinary/recipe/restaurant text.
